blocks.x: We get to the mid-seventies and the Italians ask you to start a nonet.
The what?
The Italians asked you to start a nonet as I recall.
The Italians?

Yeah. You told me this story, or Sy Johnson or somebody, that the Italian Communist party wanted you to put together a nine-piece band to do some concerts and you said “I don’t have a nonet, how about a quartet or a quintet or three trios?”
Oh yeah. I remember saying something like that.
Is that factual? Have I got that right or what?
Well, I really don’t remember those circumstances. I remember saying that though, in some context.
But you did put together a nonet that lasted for a number of years and did several records.
I started a nonet across the street here.
At Striker’s.
In seventy-three or something like that.
It was a little later I think seventy-five.
I moved here in seventy-three so it was sometime around then but I don’t remember a Communist party being responsible for that.
I remember they made you an offer to bring in a nine-piece band to Italy to do some concerts. I remember you told me that a long time ago.
It’s possible but . . .
In any case the band did begin and I guess Dave Berger had some charts.
Yeah. Dave Berger was responsible for that instrumentation. He had charts and it was his suggestion for that instrumentation.
But then you met Sy Johnson or you already knew Sy but Sy got interested in writing for the band.
Yeah. He wanted to co-lead the band.
That’s when it really took off in terms of material written for the band.
